transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we prepare for the broader rollout of the remote CI-build cache next Monday, I want to do a quick readiness check before I finalize the configuration. Could the cloud infrastructure and CI platform engineering teams share any operational details or concerns I should be aware of? Things like capacity, monitoring, failover behavior, or anything else that might affect how we configure the rollout.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While reconciling a different cloud bill this morning, I confirmed that cross-region cache reads would create about $1,200 per month in egress charges, while regional cache reads would stay within the existing build-platform budget. I haven't updated the rollout document yet, but this is important for the rollout configuration decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During a compatibility test late yesterday, I confirmed that the cache client cannot safely serve Windows runners. The rollout must exclude Windows projects and cover only Linux and macOS projects initially. I haven't filed the compatibility note yet, but this is critical for the rollout configuration decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text:
Thanks Mina and Theo — both of those are critical inputs for the rollout configuration. Let me make sure I have the details straight before I finalize the decision.

Mina: Cross-region cache reads would cost ~$1,200/month in egress, while regional cache reads stay within the existing build-platform budget. So we should configure the cache to use regional reads only to avoid the unplanned egress cost.

Theo: The cache client cannot safely serve Windows runners, so we need to exclude Windows projects from the initial rollout and cover only Linux and macOS projects.

Before I settle the configuration, a couple of follow-up questions:
1. Mina, is there any scenario where regional-only reads would cause a correctness or availability problem for any of the Linux/macOS build projects, or is it purely a cost optimization with no functional downside?
2. Theo, is there a rough timeline for when Windows compatibility might be resolved, so I can note it as a follow-up commitment?

Once I hear back, I'll finalize the rollout configuration.

transcript.text: To answer your first question, Riley: based on what I've confirmed so far, the regional-only reads recommendation is purely a cost optimization to avoid the ~$1,200/month in unplanned egress charges. I have not been given any information suggesting that regional-only reads would cause a correctness or availability problem for Linux/macOS build projects. That said, I can only speak to the cost data I verified this morning — I don't have visibility into whether there are any Linux/macOS projects that specifically depend on cross-region cache availability, so if Theo or the CI platform team has insight on that, it would be worth confirming.

To answer your second question, Riley: I don't have a timeline for Windows compatibility resolution yet. The compatibility issue was only confirmed late yesterday, and I haven't had a chance to investigate the root cause or scope a fix. I'll file the compatibility note today and can provide a follow-up estimate once I've looked into it further.

Regarding Mina's point about cross-region cache availability for Linux/macOS projects: I don't have any information suggesting that Linux or macOS projects specifically depend on cross-region cache reads. The compatibility testing I performed covered Linux and macOS runners and did not surface any cross-region dependency concerns. That said, my testing focused on client compatibility, not on whether any individual project's build workflow assumes cross-region cache availability, so I can't rule it out entirely.
